cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: EngageLab lets AI agents automatically answer email replies
stories.plain: EngageLab has shipped a feature letting AI agents handle inbound email replies autonomously — not just send outbound messages. This is a meaningful step toward agentic email marketing, where the system reads, decides, and responds without a human in the loop. Marketers evaluating automation platforms need to understand what governance guardrails come with that capability.

stories.head: Cuttable data: 1 in 11 Meta ads delivers 10x return on spend
stories.plain: Cuttable's analysis of Meta ad performance finds a dramatic concentration of returns — only about 9% of ads hit 10x ROAS. For marketers using AI to allocate paid budgets, this signals that bandit-style exploration and ruthless pruning of underperformers is more valuable than broad spend. It reframes how AI-driven budget optimisation should be configured.

stories.head: Expert view: Hidden manual work inside 'automated' marketing operations
stories.plain: Linnworks CMO Hilary Smith argues that most so-called automated marketing stacks still rely on unseen manual labour to function. For teams buying or building AI-powered martech, this is a governance and due-diligence warning: vendor automation claims often obscure human dependencies that create risk when campaign promises hit operational reality.

stories.head: Madhive selects AdImpact to add competitive spend intelligence to local media
stories.plain: Madhive is integrating AdImpact's competitive spend data into its local-media platform, giving broadcasters and agencies visibility into rival budgets by market. For AI-driven campaign planning tools, richer competitive signals improve decisioning quality — making this a data-layer upgrade rather than a logo deal.

stories.head: Tec-Do ships Navos Pro AI marketing tool
stories.plain: Tec-Do has launched Navos Pro, a new AI-powered marketing automation product. Details remain slim in current coverage, but its entry adds another vendor to an already crowded agentic-martech space. Buyers evaluating platforms should watch for specifics on what decisions Navos Pro makes autonomously and how those decisions are logged or audited.

stories.head: EngageLab launches Agent Email: AI agents that receive and answer inbound customer email at scale
stories.plain: Aurora Mobile's EngageLab built purpose-made infrastructure so AI agents can receive, read, and reply to inbound customer emails — not just send them. Replies stay threaded in Gmail and Outlook, are grounded in a private knowledge base, and intent signals write back to CRM. This shifts email from a broadcast tool to a two-way autonomous channel, which changes how CEPs are evaluated.

stories.head: Peec AI launches Peec Agent to help marketing teams act on how brands appear in AI search results
stories.plain: Peec AI, used by 3,500+ companies, added an agentic layer to its GEO platform that not only diagnoses how a brand is represented in AI search engines but autonomously recommends and executes fixes across technical, content, and third-party signals. This is a meaningful step toward fully automated brand visibility management inside AI answers.

stories.head: Limelit ships MCP server and autonomous content agents giving marketing teams 211 GEO workflow tools
stories.plain: Limelit's MCP server plugs Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other assistants directly into a governed GEO workflow engine that tracks visibility across six AI search engines and runs scheduled agents to turn ranking gaps into approved content. A free tier lowers the adoption barrier. It signals that GEO is becoming an automated, agent-driven discipline rather than a manual SEO cousin.

stories.head: ChatGPT sends less than 1% of Google's traffic — but converts at a higher rate
stories.plain: New data shows Google organic still drives 27 times more conversions than all LLMs combined, yet ChatGPT visitors convert at a notably higher rate per visit. For marketers debating GEO budget, this is the clearest quantitative benchmark yet: AI search volume is tiny but intent quality is high, which shapes how to prioritize investment.

stories.head: How to build a reliable source of truth for AI agents
stories.plain: AI agents follow instructions correctly but still produce wrong outputs when the documents they rely on are stale or contradictory. This practical guide addresses knowledge-base governance as the foundational requirement for safe agentic marketing systems. As more CEPs embed autonomous agents, getting the source-of-truth layer right becomes a buying and build criterion, not just an IT concern.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Take Autonomous Action Across the Stack
body: The past month marks a clear pivot from AI as a suggestion engine to AI as an autonomous operator. Tools like Limelit (211 agentic tools via MCP), EngageLab's Agent Email (which reads & replies to customers), Framer's MCP server (which builds websites on command), and AgentSpot (multi-agent coordination) all shipped in the same window — signaling that agent infrastructure is now production-ready.

For decision-makers, this changes the hiring & tooling calculus immediately. The new question is not whether to automate a task but which agent gets write-access to what system — and what guardrails govern that access. Teams that haven't mapped their data & permissions architecture will find agentic rollouts stall on governance, not capability.

themes.head: AI Search & GEO Rewrites Discoverability Rules
body: AI-powered search is no longer a future threat to SEO — it is the present buying environment. Prompts are replacing queries, and brands that don't appear in AI-generated answers are invisible at the research stage. Creator content is emerging as a surprising lever: AI recommendation engines disproportionately surface products that have rich, credible third-party content behind them, shifting influencer ROI from awareness to conversion.

The CommerceIQ CEO's framing that 'discoverability is the new shelf' crystallises the strategic shift: retail media, product content, and search optimisation must now be managed as one integrated system rather than separate channel budgets. Teams still measuring success by keyword rank alone are optimising for a game that has already changed.

themes.head: Personalization Shifts to Behavioral Intent, Not Identity
body: A quiet but consequential reframe is underway: the most effective personalisation no longer anchors on who a customer is (demographics, CRM profile) but on what they are trying to do in the moment. This matters practically because it sidesteps many identity-resolution & consent headaches while delivering relevance at the point of intent — aligning with both privacy trends and the rise of AI-driven, context-aware recommendation.

Paired with the push to move from journeys to real-time decisions, this theme signals that linear funnel models are obsolete infrastructure. Marketers need decision-logic layers — not just segmentation — and the data architecture to feed them signals fast enough to matter.
ev: MarTech · AI source of truth for agents

themes.head: Composable Architecture Becomes Non-Negotiable
body: Composable martech — assembling best-of-breed components via APIs rather than buying monolithic suites — is crossing from early-adopter to mainstream expectation. The driver is AI: agent-based workflows require clean, modular data and tool interfaces that legacy all-in-one platforms were never designed to expose. GeeLark's API/CLI/MCP expansion and Framer's MCP server are product bets that composability is the new baseline.

The strategic implication for buyers is to audit vendor lock-in risk now, before agentic workflows are embedded deeply. Platforms that cannot expose their data & actions via standard interfaces will become bottlenecks, while those that do become connective tissue across an organisation's AI stack.
ev: Agile Brand · Manual work inside automation

themes.head: Measurement & Skills Gaps Constrain AI's Real Return
body: Even as AI tooling accelerates, two systemic constraints are slowing real value capture: dashboards that can't answer strategic questions (the CEO problem) & teams whose skills haven't kept pace with the tools they've been handed. Adding more AI licenses or headcount without reskilling is explicitly called out as a losing strategy — the gap is interpretive & judgment-based, not tool-based.

Measurement frameworks are also cracking under pressure: voice-of-the-customer programmes need reinvention, AI's retention impact is hard to isolate, and the revelation that ChatGPT sends less than 1% of Google's traffic is a useful reality check against hype-driven budget shifts. Teams that instrument AI investments with clear, comparable metrics before scaling will separate from those chasing headlines.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack, the shift from AI as assistant to AI as autonomous operator is already underway — and the teams that will win are those that fix their data architecture, measurement discipline, and skills base before the agents arrive.
